title: Performance, Scalability, and Latency
summary: Tell the difference between a system that is slow for one person and one that cannot keep up with many.
keyPoints: Performance is how fast one request feels; scalability is how well the system handles more work.
Latency is time per action; throughput is actions per unit of time.
Concurrency, throughput, and latency are linked: concurrency ≈ throughput × latency.
Averages hide slow users, so track p50, p95, and p99.
Scale up for a quick ceiling, and scale out for long-run growth and failure tolerance.

complexity.note: Measure the real workload, not a tiny benchmark.
The average hides the slowest requests.
The database often becomes the limit first.

commonMistakes: Calling every slowdown a scalability problem without checking whether a single request is already slow.
Reporting only the average latency and missing a long p99 tail.
Adding application servers when the shared database is the bottleneck.
Sizing a connection pool from average traffic while ignoring bursts and slow queries.
interviewNotes: State whether the symptom appears for one user or only under load; the fix differs.
Put a number on the target: for example, p95 under 200 ms at 3x expected peak.
Use Little's Law out loud to justify worker and connection-pool sizes.
Name the first shared bottleneck you expect and how you would protect it.

checkYourself.question: What is the difference between a performance problem and a scalability problem?
checkYourself.answer: A performance problem is slow for one user. A scalability problem is acceptable for one user but gets slow as load grows, because capacity does not grow with demand.

checkYourself.question: Why can a page have a much worse p99 than every service it calls?
checkYourself.answer: The page waits for the slowest dependency. Even a small chance of a slow response in each service becomes a larger chance that at least one call is slow.

checkYourself.question: How many requests are in flight at 500 requests per second with a 200 ms response time?
checkYourself.answer: 500 × 0.2 = 100 requests in flight on average. Size pools for the peak, not only the average.
